record.original_question: Can the empirical success of the subspace-completion method in Wigner distribution deconvolution be justified by rigorous theory that proves when and why it reconstructs the signal correctly?

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. Can the performance of SC be theoretically justified?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $f \in \mathbb{C}^d$ be an unknown signal (the object) and let $w \in \mathbb{C}^d$ be a known window/probe. For shifts $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ and frequencies $k \in \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$, the (discrete) ptychographic / short-time Fourier transform measurements are
$$Y[k,\ell] \;=\; \Big|\sum_{n=0}^{d-1} f[n]\, \overline{w[n-\ell]}\, e^{-2\pi i k n/d}\Big|^2.$$
The Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD) approach takes the 2D discrete Fourier transform of $Y$ in both variables and, after dividing by the (assumed nonvanishing) corresponding transform of the probe's ambiguity function, recovers entries of the rank-one lifted matrix $F = f f^* \in \mathbb{C}^{d\times d}$ along its diagonals. When some diagonals of $F$ are unmeasured or unreliable (e.g. because the probe's ambiguity transform vanishes or is small on the corresponding frequencies), the *subspace-completion (SC) method* fills in the missing diagonals by exploiting the rank-one (or low-rank) structure: it projects the partially recovered matrix onto the set of rank-one Hermitian matrices, or equivalently completes the missing diagonals by a least-squares fit to the principal eigenvector subspace determined by the recovered diagonals. Empirically, SC reconstructs $f$ (up to a global phase) accurately even when a nontrivial set of diagonals is missing.

Problem. Provide a rigorous theoretical justification of the subspace-completion method for WDD. Specifically, identify explicit, verifiable conditions on the probe $w$, on the dimension $d$, and on the set $S \subset \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ of measured (reliable) diagonals of $F = ff^*$ under which the subspace-completion procedure provably recovers $f$ up to a global unimodular phase, and quantify the stability of the reconstruction with respect to additive measurement noise (i.e. derive error bounds of the form $\min_{|c|=1}\|\hat f - c f\| \le C(w,d,S)\,\|\text{noise}\|$ with explicit constants).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of a rigorous theoretical foundation for the subspace-completion (SC) method in Wigner distribution deconvolution appears to remain open. Existing works (e.g., Forstner–Krahmer–Melnyk–Sissouno on "well-conditioned ptychographic imaging via lost subspace completion," and related WDD analyses) establish uniqueness and stability for WDD itself and propose subspace-completion procedures, but a complete theoretical justification—precise conditions on probe and missing diagonals guaranteeing exact and stable recovery via SC—has not been fully established in the published literature found.

status_evidence.title: Well conditioned ptychographic imaging via lost subspace completion
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces lost subspace completion for ptychography but does not provide complete theoretical guarantees for the SC method as commonly used in WDD.
status_evidence.claim: Subspace-completion has been proposed and partially analyzed but a fully rigorous justification of when and why it works is not established.

status_evidence.title: Denoised Wigner distribution deconvolution via low-rank matrix completion
status_evidence.snippet: Uses low-rank matrix completion within WDD; proves recovery in certain regimes but leaves open conditions for general SC variants.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical results exist for related low-rank completion variants but not a complete theory for SC.

status_evidence.title: Background Removal for Ptychography via Wigner Distribution Deconvolution
status_evidence.snippet: Discards corrupted equations of the WDD linear system and recovers lost information using redundancy; theoretical recovery analysis is partial.
status_evidence.claim: Recent SIAM J. Imaging Sciences work uses SC-like procedures but theoretical justification is incomplete.
